samples.summary: New Parquet entry point reaches applyContent with no cell budget, bypassing the MAX_IMPORT_CELLS invariant that protects the Yorkie document size ceiling
samples.evidence: MAX_IMPORT_CELLS = 40_000 (packages/sheets/src/import/csv-importer.ts:155) exists to keep an import under Yorkie's per-document byte ceiling - packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/csv-doc-size.test.ts:11 says so and derives the number from worst-case per-cell CRDT cost. The only pre-import gate on the new path is uploadSizeError (packages/frontend/src/app/documents/file-meta.ts:34-48), which allows any non-image file up to 50 MB. importParquet then calls importParquetFile -> importRecordsAsSheet (packages/sheets/src/import/record-importer.ts:37), which writes every record unconditionally, and packages/frontend/src/app/documents/upload-queue.ts:351-359 persists the result through applyContent. Parquet is columnar and compressed, so a well-under-cap file can decode to millions of cells: browser OOM or a doc that cannot be persisted, with no truncated signal (upload-queue.ts:367 can only report truncation for the CSV path). The JSON path shares the gap, but uncompressed text makes 50 MB a far tighter bound than 50 MB of Parquet.

samples.summary: Routing hyparquet/fzstd/hysnappy into the sheet-core chunk makes the Parquet decoder eagerly loaded by every spreadsheet consumer, defeating the dynamic import in parquet-importer.ts
samples.evidence: manualChunks also routes /packages/sheets/src/{view,model,store}/ to "sheet-core" (packages/frontend/vite.config.ts:202-208), and those modules are statically imported by the spreadsheet surface. Once the Parquet reader and its codecs are placed in the same chunk, that chunk is fetched whenever a spreadsheet opens, so the await import('hyparquet') in packages/sheets/src/import/parquet-importer.ts:17-20 no longer defers any bytes - it only defers execution. Consumers of sheet-core other than the import path (every sheet editor session, and any docs/slides code pulling sheets model/store) now pay for hyparquet + fzstd + hysnappy. The per-chunk KB gate will catch a hard budget break, but not the eager-load regression while it stays under the limit.

samples.summary: Contract comments enumerating which importers can report truncated/rowCount were not updated for the new Parquet path
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/sheet-import-actions.ts:17-24 documents "Only the CSV path can report these - the XLSX and JSON importers read their input whole", and packages/frontend/src/app/documents/upload-queue.ts:360-363 repeats "Only the CSV path has a budget; the other sheet formats report neither field". Parquet is now a third whole-file importer that reports neither field; both comments describe the pre-change format list, so the next reader has to re-derive which paths are budgeted.

samples.summary: Design docs still record Parquet import as unshipped / DuckDB-only after this change ships the client-side path
samples.evidence: docs/design/sheets/file-import.md:30 has a status row "Parquet / JSON import | none | -", and docs/design/README.md:24 summarises the doc as "adds CSV (papaparse) + Parquet/JSON via DuckDB". With importParquetFile wired into importSheetFile and classifyUploadKind, the shipped state is client-side hyparquet for local .parquet files, so these tables now describe the old world. The nested-doc reference check does not recurse into docs/design/<topic>/, so nothing else flags this.

samples.summary: This is the first runtime dynamic import in packages/sheets, which changes the library build output shape for the dist consumers (backend runtime)
samples.evidence: Grep for 'import(' under packages/sheets/src returns only parquet-importer.ts:18-19 (the other hit, sheet.ts:3105, is a type-only import type). packages/sheets/vite.build.ts builds es+cjs lib bundles with only 'assert' and 'util' external, so hyparquet/hyparquet-compressors are bundled and the new dynamic import introduces a code-split point (or gets inlined) in both formats. packages/backend/package.json:43 depends on the built package and its runtime resolves dist/wafflebase-sheet.cjs, so the stated goal in parquet-importer.ts:15-16 (keeping browser-only ESM deps out of server-side consumers) depends on how Rollup emits that split - worth verifying the built dist actually loads under Node/Jest before relying on the comment.
searchedFor: Grep @wafflebase/sheets in package.json files and packages/backend

verdict.reason: Verified the whole chain independently. MAX_IMPORT_CELLS is real and enforced only inside the CSV writer (csv-importer.ts:155, :288), with csv-doc-size.test.ts:11,107 documenting it as the guard against Yorkie's per-document byte ceiling. The Parquet entry point (sheet-import-actions.ts:118-127) calls parquet-importer.ts:21, which decodes every row with no limit, then record-importer.ts:57-74, which writes every non-empty cell unconditionally and returns no truncation signal. The path is reachable: upload-kind.ts:27 classifies .parquet as "sheet", so upload-queue.ts:349-359 runs importSheetFile and persists the result via applyContent, which overwrites the Yorkie root wholesale (apply-imported-content.ts:213-217). The only pre-import gate is uploadSizeError at upload-queue.ts:90 -> file-meta.ts:22,45-47, a byte cap of 50 MB for non-images, which is not cell-based and is very loose for compressed columnar data. upload-queue.ts:367 can only report truncation when `truncated` is set, which this path never sets. I searched for a second gate: repo-wide grep of MAX_/LIMIT/cellCount across packages/sheets/src and packages/frontend/src (xlsx-importer has only a bare counter, no cap), repo-wide grep of "parquet" in all src files (only the files above plus index.ts re-exports and tests), and read applyImportedContent's sheet branch — no cell or byte budget exists anywhere on the Parquet path. This is in the blast-radius lane: a new entry point reaching the protected persist operation without passing the budget that the existing path enforces, with impact of browser OOM or an unpersistable document and no user-visible truncation signal. Major.
